chapters.html:
It began as an uncharacteristically lazy day for Mydei, which should have been the first sign that something was wrong.

Early morning training went as it usually did, save for the absence of one Deliverer– Mydei had noted his absence and thought nothing of it, as Aglaea had every Chrysos Heir running ragged with little quests to complete– Titankin to slay, villagers to save– all in a day's work. So he trained, shared a meal with his people, and then… Nothing.

There was nothing of grand import to do today. No missions to be sent out on, no meetings to attend, no soldiers that required his training, no scholars that required his knowledge on Kremnoan history… Hell, even the children that enjoyed clinging to his chiton to demand his attention were busy with their studies for the day! And most notably of all, there was no Deliverer to pester him for another match, another outing, another moment of your time, dear prince. Come now. Won't you indulge me in another bout? Scared to lose?

Mydei shakes his head to physically dislodge the memory. How could he spend his free time thinking of the Deliverer? He already spent all of his free time with the man. Instead, he should use the time to do literally anything else– anything would be more productive than wondering how his mission is going, how long it would take him to return to Okhema, why the man hadn't even told Mydei he was leaving when he was certain that they'd made a pact to inform the other if they were leaving on quests, just in case the other required assistance, or in case the mission went south–

He's doing it again. Mydei runs a frustrated hand through his hair. Perhaps he should partake in some fare from the diner he often frequents– No, he and Phainon regularly share meals there, and the servers will be sure to ask where the man is. Alright, then… He should visit Marmoreal Market and peruse the wares– No, he'd share the exact same problem as with the diner! Every vendor would be asking after Phainon! They loved to spoil that man with deals and samples…

Urgh. How frustrating that a single man could be so loud and occupy so much space even in his absence!

Mydei decides to just retreat to his chambers and have a nice nap. He hasn't done so in so very long, and there was no way that the Deliverer could torment him even in his dreams, right? Right.

So he settles down onto his cushions and throws an arm over his eyes in a futile attempt to keep Okhema's unending day from disrupting his slumber. Oddly enough, he falls asleep quite easily– and has a strange dream about… punching someone in the face? While in a kitchen?

“Mydei!”

Mydei tosses and turns. No, the face of the person he's punched is blurry, and he'd like to see it. Besides, he hasn't slept so well in so long. If he squints, maybe he can make out fluffy hair…

“Hey! Get up!”

Blue eyes, a fair complexion…

“Hellooooo~? Crown prince! Help! There's a damsel in need of rescuing!”

Mydei sits up, bleary from sleep. Was that the Deliverer that he punched? In his dreams as well? Could the Deliverer stop running through his mind, or what? Were the two of them simply fated to encounter one another even in dreams? Perhaps Mydei should get another hobby that wouldn't involve that man showing up and asserting himself.

…No, knowing Phainon, it would be impossible. When Mydei cooks, he appears. When Mydei bathes, he appears. Phainon, Phainon, Phainon!

“Mrgh,” he grumbles.

“Woah, that worked,” a voice exclaims. It's the one of the Trailblazers, Caelus, and his fluffy pink squirrel. “You're just missing a white horse and a cool sword, oh crown prince.”

“...What?”

“Nothing, really.” Caelus says, smiling wide. “Don't ask questions. Come with us! This is a kidnapping!”

The young man takes Mydei by the wrist and starts running out of the room. And just when Mydei finally gains enough awareness to realize that he may truly be in the process of being kidnapped, Caelus has dragged him to their destination, the… Square in front of Marmoreal Palace?

There's a small crowd gathered, forming a circle around someone that he can't quite make out, on account of the rabble. But he can spot the Ladies Tribios, Castorice and Hyacine, and that other Trailblazer, Dan Heng, too… Plus a handful of others pretending that they aren't watching the ongoing commotion.

“Agy and Naxy shall be here shortly,” Mydei hears Tribbie say. “They're busy bickering over the origins of this curse. Once they're done gazing into each other's eyes like they don't want to make out, they'll be here! They won't want to miss this. And Little Gray is bringing De, of course…”

Curse?

Caelus drags him to the center of the crowd, where someone has haphazardly dragged over a daybed. A daybed that the Deliverer has passed out on.

“Phainon?” Mydei hears himself blurt. A hush falls over the crowd as Mydei frees himself from Caelus’ grasp and hurries to the Deliverer’s side. “What happened?!”

He checks for breathing. Steady. And then a pulse. Slow, but even steadier. No visible wounds, either. The man simply looks to be asleep, but would there be a crowd if he was simply sleeping? Mydei looks to the triplets for an answer, and then Hyacine as well.

Oddly enough, the crowd is smothering giggles. Mydei can feel his face drop. “Is the Deliverer attempting to prank me again?” The prince asks, voice even.

“No,” Dan Heng says.

“It’s happening,” Caelus says, at the same time. He sounds way too pleased. Is that a camera in his hands?

Castorice folds her hands in front of her. “No, Lord Mydei. We have need of your assistance. You see…”

She trails off, eyes darting to the side. In fact, now that Mydei's noticing it, everyone's… Fidgeting. Odd. But if it wasn't a prank, then what was it?

“Snowy’s been cursed and he won't wake up!” Tribbie declares, waving her arms around. “We need your help, De!”

Mydei's heart sputters against the cage of his chest. “What? Explain!”

The long and short of it is this; the Deliverer had protected some fool from activating some long-dormant trap to prove his thesis by… allowing himself to be hit by its effects instead. Yes. How very like the Deliverer to suffer the consequences of his hero complex. The details are convoluted, but long story short, as the Lady Tribbie explains, it was a trap devised by Mnestia and Zagreus, of all the possible cursed combinations. Confirmed by Aglaea, the professor Anaxa, and Cipher, who was busy destroying what remained of the aforementioned trap, there was nothing that they could do but drag Phainon's body back to Okhema and wait for the cure.

Mydei cannot possibly begin to understand how the two Titans decided to conspire like that. He supposes he didn't need to understand. He just needed to fix this.

“Shall I go and destroy the remnants of the trap with Lady Cipher?” Mydei asks, already adjusting his gauntlets in preparation for a long and arduous battle. Who knows what trials Mnestia and Zagreus would make one undergo in order to counter one of their curses? “Slay a monster? Retrieve ancient texts to find the cure? Point me the way, Lady Tribbie. We need to do what we can to get this fool back on his feet.”

Tribbie, Trianne, and Trinnon all make Xs simultaneously with their arms. “It's alright, De!” Tribbie says, oddly bright for someone discussing a curse. “We already know how to cure Snowy.”

Mydei frowns. “Should I seek out an ingredient, or potion, then…?” He asks, genuinely confused at all the smiles he's getting. Hyacine is giggling into her hand. Caelus isn't even bothering to hide his laughter, even when Dan Heng tries to shush him. Hells, even Castorice looks far too amused for the situation at hand. “What is it? What does he need?”

“We have the cure,” Trinnon reiterates, voice as soft as ever.

“Then why hasn't anyone used it?” Mydei demands, his chest growing hot with offense. While everyone was laughing, Phainon was–

“The cure is…” Tribbie pauses for dramatic effect. “True Love's kiss!”

…Huh?

Was Mydei still half-asleep? Did she just say…

True Love's kiss?

“That's why we haven't been able to wake him yet!” Trianne adds. “Because we were waiting for his one True Love to come to the rescue!”

Indignation quickly fades away to confusion. “...Are you making fun of me?” Mydei wonders, feeling lost.

“Nuh-uh!” The triplets declare as one. Mydei looks to the others for help. They all shrug at him, barely fighting off their smiles.

“True Love's kiss isn't a real thing,” Mydei tries, still in disbelief that this isn't a prank. “It's a concept in stories for children. Pure fiction.”

“Nuh uh,” Trianne denies. “Agy confirmed that True Love's kiss is a real thing.”

“And is the Lady Aglaea the leading expert on the matter?” Mydei asks.

Everyone looks at him strangely. It's enough to fluster him. “Who else if not Agy?” Tribbie counters. You know what? Fair enough. “Besides, we have actual documented records on this sorta thing. Married couples and friends and such being hit by this curse. You see?”

Mydei did not, in fact, see.

“It's not the strangest thing that I've seen in my time as a Trailblazer,” Caelus adds. Dan Heng nods along. Wasn't he Caelus’ only scrap of self control and reason? Help him out, please. “In fact, it's not even the strangest thing I've seen in Okhema, dude.”

That wasn't really reassuring. Mydei brushes hair away from Phainon's face and takes a deep breath to regain his composure. “So? I assume you all know who his True Love is, since you're all quite calm. Are we waiting on them?”

He ignores the way that his chest clenches at the thought of the Deliverer’s fated love. As long as the man wakes up, Mydei should feel relieved, so what were these complex emotions muddling his mind?

“Nope! They're already here!” Tribbie points somewhere in Mydei's general direction. Confused, he turns around. No one is there. He turns back around and spots a sea of smug faces. It suddenly hits him, what everyone seems to think–

“Me!?” Mydei booms, pointing at himself.

“You,” Trinnon confirms, bobbing her head.

“Me, the Deliverer’s one True Love?!” Mydei demands. “How– How can that be?”

For some reason, it's the crowd's turn to give him a confused look. “Well, who else could it be?” Hyacine asks. “There's no one else but you.”

“But I– Huh?!” Hello? What in the world?

“You gotta smooch him! A little kiss! You know? Should be easy! Don't you guys do it all the time?”

“No?!?” Mydei sputters. “The two of us, we… We aren't even like that?!”

Confused mumbles start to build in the crowd. Mydei can even hear the congregation in the distance start going what?! and huh?! at each other when he's the one meant to be going what and huh, excuse you.

“If you're not like that, then why was I feeling like a third wheel for that entire outing we had?” Caelus demands, looking aghast.

“The entirety of Okhema feels like a third wheel whenever the two of you are out and about!” Mydei hears someone yell in the distance. He's going to ignore that for the sake of his sanity.

“What about the betting pool of when you two will get married?!” He also hears from afar. He'll ignore that, too. And how he hears a whole slew of people shush whoever spoke.

Castorice actually has a hand over her mouth. “I genuinely believed that the two of you were lovers this whole time,” she adds, voice soft.

Lovers?!

“We're not lovers?” It comes out as a question, for what reason.

“Then what the hell were we all subjected to?!” Mydei hears, again, from a distance.

“Still, there's no one else but you for Snowy, De,” Tribbie says, hands on her hips. “Can you honestly think of anyone else with a closer bond with him than you?”

Mydei opens his mouth… And then closes it.

Well! Well!!! Even if True Love's kiss was a thing, an actual curse-breaking thing, what the hell did that have to do with him and the Deliverer? Sure, their bond was… Indescribable, but it wasn't, like, that!

“And according to Agy, it must be on the lips! Otherwise it won't work!”

Wh–

Mydei swears that he hears something explode in the distance. Or maybe that's just his brain.

Everyone is now looking at him with expectant eyes. Somehow, even though Phainon is literally unconscious and sprawled out on the daybed, Mydei can somehow feel his sparkly gaze drilling holes through his face. Urgh.

How could Mydei make them see the truth of this matter?

“I don't think that he thinks that we're like that,” Mydei says.

“Don't be shy,” Caelus grins, catlike. He makes little kissy sounds that Dan Heng valiantly attempts to smother with his hands. Mydei is briefly grateful to the man. Though his attempts were clearly in vain, Mydei appreciated the effort. “Just think of it like first aid. CPR. Trust my expertise.”

“What expertise?” Dan Heng mumbles.

“I'm not shy!” Mydei counters. He takes a deep breath to regain his composure. “It's only– You're wrong! All of you! How could you collectively decide– I– How could I possibly be the Deliverer’s True Love? We bicker–”

“Like a married couple,” Tribbie offers.

“–and we come to blows more often than not–”

“I thought that that's just how the two of you flirt?” Hyacine adds, sounding genuinely confused.

“–I don't even think he likes men?!” Mydei blurts, not knowing why everyone is looking at him like he's the crazy one.

“Phainon's Mydei-sexual,” Caelus says, nodding at nothing and no one in particular. What. “I think it's cute. Have you ever seen a more fixated man?”

It sounds like a rhetorical question, so Mydei will simply not answer. And pretend to not have heard. He looks to the others for help.

Castorice looks like she wants to put a gentle hand on his shoulder. Instead, she tilts her head to one side. “It's okay to be embarrassed about kissing him,” she says, trying for sympathetic. It falls flat. Like her voice.

“I'M NOT EMBARRASSED.”

“We can turn around! And shut our eyes! If it makes you feel better!” Trianne blurts. She covers her eyes with her hands. This action is immediately negated by her peeking through her fingers.

Mydei shuts his eyes and takes a deep, grounding breath. “Okay. Why does everyone think that I'm the Deliverer’s one True Love? I need proof, or I am heading out on a quest to find a different cure.”

Everyone in the general vicinity exchanges glances. Mydei is seriously going to kick Phainon's ass when he wakes up, for making him go through this. “Well?”

Hyacine claps her hands together to draw his attention. “If you want examples, then what about that time that Phainon was testing that healing draught, and became all loopy?”

Oh, no. He immediately knows what she's getting at. “The Deliverer was on drugs,” Mydei instinctively protests.

“Wait, what? Spill?” Caelus blurts, at the exact same time. The two of them lock eyes, one incredibly embarrassed and the other hungry for gossip.

Hyacine's eyes practically sparkle at the chance to tell her story. “Well… This took place a few months ago, when many of our healers left the city to go support a distant village with an outbreak of Titankin. The healers that remained, like myself, decided to experiment with new healing draughts to make up for the loss in labour…”

Mydei runs a hand down his face at the memory of that day, knowing full well that everyone would take it out of context. The context being the Deliverer being not in his right mind.

Kephale, rescue him from this plight…!

.

While on his way to find the Deliverer and give him a tongue lashing for being so extraordinarily tardy to their meeting, Mydei finds Lady Hyacine awkwardly pacing the halls and fidgeting with her hair. Huh. And when they lock eyes, she yelps and covers her face with her hands, guilt seeping through every bit of her actions. She's so incredibly suspicious-looking that Mydei immediately begins to suspect that she's somehow involved with the Deliverer’s absence.

He crosses the hall to greet her and she shrinks down. Like that would stop him from seeing her.

“Have you seen the Deliverer around?” Mydei asks, folding his arms across his chest. “He promised to meet me for a meal, but he's late.”

Hyacine freezes in place, and then winces. “I'm sorry! He told me that he had plans with you, but we didn't expect our little experiment to take longer than an hour.” She gestures for him to follow, her gait wobbly. “I should have gone to tell you immediately, but I was sort of hoping that he'd just be fine before I found you.”

He shakes his head, dismissing her worries. “Experiment?” Mydei asks, already deciding not to blame her. He's sure that Phainon refused to acknowledge his limits, again, and ended up in some sticky situation. Again.

“As you know, not all of Okhema's healers are healers in the way that I am,” Hyacine explains, leading Mydei through a set of doors. “Some rely on potions, and draughts, and other such items. Due to the surge of Titankin in the west, many of our healers have been sent to meet the wounded halfway, so we've been stocking up on healing items in their absence. And, you know, while we're at it, we decided to try new formulas to see what'd work.”

Mydei frowns. “Let me guess. The Deliverer was testing one of these new formulas?”

“Yes! But he's not injured, or in any pain, just… You'll see,” she says, looking flustered. “The formula, it's meant to take away pain, make it so the patient feels nothing at all so our healers can work their magic without any additional duress. But it has, well, um. It has unforeseen side effects! Temporary loss of memory, of inhibitions… It's all temporary, I swear!”

Mydei shoots her an alarmed look. “It wears off quick!” Hyacine blurts, throwing up her hands. “Thirty minutes minimum, a day, max. Phainon thought he'd be one of the thirty minute men. He was, um, not correct.”

The healer guides him to one of the sickrooms. The beds are divided by thick curtains, and Hyacine pulls aside the closest one to reveal the Deliverer, who doesn't even look up at their sudden arrival.

“Be gentle with him,” Hyacine says. Mydei barely hears her. He's too distracted by the dazed look on Phainon's face. The Deliverer genuinely looks like there are stars spinning around his head, eyes foggy and unfocused. “His memory isn't stable. It'll return within the day, but he didn't recall my name. I'm not sure that he'll know yours. Some people can hardly remember their own name, others only lose a few memories. It all depends on the person.”

“Oh, he'll know my name,” Mydei says, lip curling. “He has no choice.” Hyacine huffs, the sound more amused than anything else.

“If you're going to scold him, then scold him when he has all his memories in order,” Hyacine urges. “This Phainon has no idea where he is, really. He'll have no idea that he even missed your date.”

Date?

Before he can correct her, Phainon finally turns to Mydei. They lock eyes.

It's… Strange. Usually, Phainon's gaze is a whole lot more intense. Keen. His eyes alone demand a challenge, like he's asking– no, demanding that Mydei gazes back with the same amount of passion. Look at me, look at me, look at me, the Deliverer would demand, somehow, with his eyes alone. Don't look away.

The current Phainon looks incredibly silly in comparison. Like some happy-go-lucky chimera who knows nothing but treats and cuddles.

“Oh, you're…”

Mydei ignores his languid words. “Deliverer. Do you have anything to say for yourself?” In the background, he hears Hyacine groan playfully.

Phainon does not have anything to say for himself on account of him immediately bursting into tears.

Naturally, Mydei panics at the unfamiliar sight. Tears?! From Phainon, of all people?! The man who would rather perish than show the citizens any sort of weakness?! Who laughs off battle wounds and injuries so people don't worry for him?!

Mydei's chest begins to ache. Strangely enough, every tear feels akin to a blade through his chest.

“Why are you crying?” The prince demands, truly at a loss for what to do. He leans forward and wipes away his tears with a gentle thumb. “Lady Hyacine! Something is wrong!”

Before Hyacine can even think to step in, Phainon speaks.

“You're so beautiful and I don't know your name,” Phainon sobs. Mydei freezes. “Waaah!”

Hyacine snorts and slaps a hand over her mouth at the sound. “Loss of inhibitions,” she explains. “I did say it.”

She did, but Mydei didn't exactly expect the Deliverer to act like this. “Don't cry,” Mydei says, because what else can he say. “Your tears are unnecessary. There is nothing to cry about, Deliverer…”

“Who are you? Why do I feel this way?” Phainon continues to weep, like he hasn't heard. “You're… You're so everything.”

That sentence didn't even make sense.

Mydei can't look away from the tears streaming down Phainon's face. Whenever he brushes them away, the man only seems to get more and more weepy.

“I am called Mydeimos,” Mydei says, feeling as though someone's put a spell on him. Like he'd do anything at all to stop Phainon from shedding tears.

“Mydeimos,” Phainon croons, sinking into the sheets. He's stopped crying, now. “Mydeimos, Mydeimos, Mydeimos. Even your name contains multitudes. Multitudes of beauty. Like your face and body.”

What the hell did that even mean. Mydei turns to Hyacine. “Are you sure that he doesn't have any head trauma? Maybe he was hiding an injury,” he suggests, voice a tad shrill.

“There's no head trauma,” Hyacine says, giggling. Well, Mydei's glad that someone is having fun in this situation.

“There is head trauma!” Phainon blurts.

“Right,” Mydei says, sitting on the side of the mattress.

“No, really,” Phainon continues, leaning forward. “When I saw you, the world started spinning.” Okay, was that a compliment or an insult?

“Uh huh,” Mydei says, suddenly amused himself. “And what do you want me to do about that?”

“I think that if I bury my face in your chest I'll be allllll better,” Phainon says, starry-eyed.

Ha.

Mydei leans forward, steals the pillow from behind Phainon's back, and attempts to smother the Deliverer with it.

“I'll bury you in something, you HKS–!”

“WAAAIT!” Hyacine yelps, leaping forward to grab the pillow. Mydei is undeterred, but Phainon is slippery, and wriggles around on the mattress like a worm. “He doesn't mean it! Lord Mydei, please, he's delusional!”

“I mean it,” Phainon gasps, taking huge gulps of air when he can. “I've never meant anything more…!”

“Oh yeah?!” Mydei bellows, face aflame. He punctuates every word with a slap of the pillow. Feathers fly everywhere. “I'm going to– Grant your wish– And slay you– Right here!”

“I'd let you slay me,” Phainon continues, tone still dreamy and utterly unaffected by the assault via pillow. “If you promise to hold me tight the whole time. To your chest. If you're feeling nice. I hope you are. Are you?”

Mydei's face burns with the force of his embarrassment. He brings down the pillow again, and somehow, it explodes.

Sudden silence fills the room, and Mydei is suddenly aware that everyone is staring. Curtains are pulled to the side, people are peeking around the doors, and Hyacine looks incredibly unimpressed with him. Whoops.

So Hyacine drags him outside of the room and scolds him for a bit. Says that while it's perfectly understandable to be flustered by his words, that he shouldn't disturb the other patients, as most of them truly are recovering from an ailment.

“Still, I understand your reaction, Lord Mydei. If you're really uncomfortable with him right now, you should make yourself scarce. You can absolutely make him pay for his inappropriate words. …After he recovers,” Hyacine says, contrite. “Please don't actually fight in the sickbay.”

Mydei makes a face. “...It's fine if it's the Deliverer saying these things. If it were anyone else, I would have already dragged them out for a duel over my honour.”

The prince knows that the Deliverer doesn't mean anything by it. And Mydei's well aware that Phainon’s incredibly loopy. He wouldn't punish the man too much for his words when he's so clearly not himself– he wouldn't have gone for the pillow otherwise.

“I can tolerate his nonsense,” he adds. “I already do, even when he's not deluded. Don't fret.” Just the other day Phainon asked him if they would still be rivals if he was a worm, which… What?

“...Oh?” Hyacine says. Her expression clears up. “Oh…! Oh! I completely understand. Congratulations! I'm genuinely happy for you both!”

Mydei would like to know what she's understood, because personally, he's confused. But before he can ask, she barrels on.

“Please indulge Phainon as much as you can, then,” Hyacine implores, a smile on her face. “Some patients have had unpleasant reactions when told that what they currently believe is incorrect. Their confusion, mixed with their loss of memory and lack of inhibition resulted in some minor, um, freakouts. Physical ones. We wouldn't want a Chrysos Heir to do the same, especially in the sickbay.”

Right, Mydei can imagine the chaos now. He nods. “Understood.”

“I should go check on the other patients,” Hyacine says, hands on her hips. “I'll leave him in your hands. Congratulations again!”

She quite literally skips back into the room before Mydei can ask what she's congratulating him for. Deciding to just ignore it, Mydei returns to the room as well, pulls back the curtain, and finds Phainon struggling to remain upright against the wall.

“HKS,” Mydei scolds, immediately putting his arms around him, “what do you think you're doing? You're not supposed to leave your bed when you're feeble. Sit back down.”

Phainon immediately attempts to sit on the floor at the command, nearly bringing Mydei down with him. The prince curses. “On the bed, you fool! I didn't say right here!”

“But you told me to sit,” Phainon whines, looking up at him with watery blue eyes. Still, he allows Mydei to drag him back to his bed and tuck him under the blanket with minimal complaints.

“Where were you even planning to go?” Mydei asks, raising an eyebrow.

“I wanted to find you,” Phainon says. He still sounds like he's talking through a dream. “You left. Why would I stay?”

Mydei shakes his head. “Focus on recovering, HKS. Don't do anything foolish.”

“I'm nooot HKS. That's not my name,” Phainon pouts. “I'm Phainon. That's me. Can you say my name? Pleaseee? Please, Mydeimos?”

Mydei can't help but be amused. “Can't you be both?”

Phainon stares at him, clearly processing the information. “I can be both,” he finally allows. “If you want me to be both. I can be HKS Phainon. That's my name now.”

Mydei grins.

“What are we to one another?” Phainon asks, an expectant look on his face. “Looking at you is like, wow. Wow.”

That was a loaded question. It was already difficult to explain their relationship to anyone, even when Phainon wasn't addled. Friends? Colleagues? Neither of those sounded right. Perhaps comrades?

“Rivals,” Mydei decides. “And partners.”

“Partners?!” Phainon repeats, voice cracking. “Oh wow. How'd I do that? Go me.”
